questions.q: The editorial names a “human contribution” of Stephen Hawking. What was it?
options: He showed that a person with a severe disability can achieve what others do, using the mind and technology
Yes. He ended the “disabled theory.”
He refused all help from others
Not quite. The article says: He showed that a person with a severe disability can achieve what others do, using the mind and technology.
He founded hospitals for the paralysed
Not quite. The article says: He showed that a person with a severe disability can achieve what others do, using the mind and technology.
He invented the wheelchair he used
Not quite. The article says: He showed that a person with a severe disability can achieve what others do, using the mind and technology.
questions.rationale: “He put an end to the ‘disabled theory’, as Dr. Hawking was a living example who proved that one who has a challenging disability can overcome it.”

questions.q: Why does the editorial find the search for a single theory of nature significant for religion?
options: It makes prayer unnecessary
Not quite. The article says: A universe governed by one unified law is like a scientific affirmation of the concept of one God.
It shows the universe has no beginning
Not quite. The article says: A universe governed by one unified law is like a scientific affirmation of the concept of one God.
It proves science and religion never meet
Not quite. The article says: A universe governed by one unified law is like a scientific affirmation of the concept of one God.
A universe governed by one unified law is like a scientific affirmation of the concept of one God
Well reasoned. Harmony points to oneness.
questions.rationale: “It is this explanation which is the equivalent of a scientific affirmation of the concept of one God.”

questions.article: The Concept of Social Welfare in Islam
questions.q: How does the article describe zakat “in spirit” and “in its external form”?
options: In spirit a tax; in form a gift
Not quite. The article says: In spirit an act of worship; in form a social service.
In spirit an act of worship; in form a social service
Right. Not merely a tax.
In spirit a custom; in form a law
Not quite. The article says: In spirit an act of worship; in form a social service.
In spirit a loan; in form a duty
Not quite. The article says: In spirit an act of worship; in form a social service.
questions.rationale: “In spirit, zakat is an act of worship, while in its external form, it is the carrying out of a social service.”

questions.article: Religion: A Divine, Not a Social Phenomenon
questions.q: Nuclear energy is judged as a fact of nature, not by how one country uses it. What does the article conclude about understanding Islam?
options: It should be understood from the Quran and Hadith, not from the conduct of any group of its followers
Yes. Theory must be told apart from practice.
It cannot be understood by outsiders
Not quite. The article says: It should be understood from the Quran and Hadith, not from the conduct of any group of its followers.
It should be understood from newspapers
Not quite. The article says: It should be understood from the Quran and Hadith, not from the conduct of any group of its followers.
It should be understood from the history of empires
Not quite. The article says: It should be understood from the Quran and Hadith, not from the conduct of any group of its followers.
questions.rationale: “Now one begins to look at Islam in the light of Quran and Hadith, instead of in the light of the practice of Muslims.”

questions.q: According to the Hadith quoted, what is the best gift a father can give his children?
options: A large inheritance
Not quite. The article says: The cultivation of good morals – preparing them to live rightly.
The cultivation of good morals – preparing them to live rightly
Correct. Pampering is called the worst gift.
The best schooling money can buy
Not quite. The article says: The cultivation of good morals – preparing them to live rightly.
Freedom from every hardship
Not quite. The article says: The cultivation of good morals – preparing them to live rightly.
questions.rationale: “There is no better and superior gift that a father can give to his children than cultivation of good morals.”

questions.q: The phrase Allahu Akbar is heard and said some three hundred times a day. What does the article say this repetition is meant to achieve?
options: To mark the passing hours
Not quite. The article says: To make God’s greatness a constant part of one’s consciousness, which makes a person modest.
To make God’s greatness a constant part of one’s consciousness, which makes a person modest
Right. It is “the essence of faith.”
To help in counting the prayers
Not quite. The article says: To make God’s greatness a constant part of one’s consciousness, which makes a person modest.
To call others to attention
Not quite. The article says: To make God’s greatness a constant part of one’s consciousness, which makes a person modest.
questions.rationale: “God’s greatness should be an integral part of his consciousness in such a way that under no condition should he lose awareness of it.”

questions.q: Besides repaying what parents have given, what further benefit does the article see in serving them?
options: It frees one from other duties
Not quite. The article says: It teaches one to look on all people with love and so to serve humanity at large.
It secures a share of their property
Not quite. The article says: It teaches one to look on all people with love and so to serve humanity at large.
It teaches one to look on all people with love and so to serve humanity at large
Well read. Home is the first school of service.
It earns the respect of neighbours
Not quite. The article says: It teaches one to look on all people with love and so to serve humanity at large.
questions.rationale: “Serving parents enables one to look at all human beings with love, it will inculcate the attitude of honouring them thus making one to serve humanity at large.”

questions.q: People in sudden danger commonly cry out to God. What does the article take this to show?
options: That people copy what others do
Not quite. The article says: That awareness of God is woven into human nature.
That awareness of God is woven into human nature
Yes. The call to God turns this potential into reality.
That danger is always a punishment
Not quite. The article says: That awareness of God is woven into human nature.
That fear makes people irrational
Not quite. The article says: That awareness of God is woven into human nature.
questions.rationale: “This proves that the concept of God is interwoven in human nature. Every human being is potentially aware of God’s existence.”

questions.q: A young man felt his prayers went unanswered. With what comparison does the article reply?
options: A farmer who must wait for rain
Not quite. The article says: A student cannot dictate his examination paper; God decides each person’s test and knows what is best.
A merchant who must bargain
Not quite. The article says: A student cannot dictate his examination paper; God decides each person’s test and knows what is best.
A traveller who has lost his way
Not quite. The article says: A student cannot dictate his examination paper; God decides each person’s test and knows what is best.
A student cannot dictate his examination paper; God decides each person’s test and knows what is best
Exactly. So pray: “Give me what is best for me.”
questions.rationale: “A student appearing for an examination cannot demand that the examination paper should be as he wants it to be… If our supplications do not appear to be accepted, we must know that this is what God wills.”

questions.q: A stone a boy was playing with turned out to be a large diamond. What does the article say about human abilities?
options: Talent is found mostly in small towns
Not quite. The article says: Hidden talents need recognising – by honest self-awareness or by a sincere well-wisher.
Hidden talents need recognising – by honest self-awareness or by a sincere well-wisher
Well reasoned. Both are rare, so much potential is lost.
Talents always show themselves in time
Not quite. The article says: Hidden talents need recognising – by honest self-awareness or by a sincere well-wisher.
Only the wealthy can develop talent
Not quite. The article says: Hidden talents need recognising – by honest self-awareness or by a sincere well-wisher.
questions.rationale: “These skills and abilities are hidden. They don’t loudly announce themselves. They need a 'lapidary' to recognize them.”
